_note: THE CONTENT UNIT IS AN INCIDENT PACKAGE, NOT AN ANOMALY (GDD 15.1). An anomaly file holds rules and nothing about where; a map file holds geometry and nothing about what happened. This binds the two, and it is the only reason two different incidents can share one floor — which is exactly what the vertical slice asks for (26.2). It carries the things that belong to neither on their own: where the thing starts, what is lying about to be found, and the briefing the squad is read.

briefing.headline: Missing maintenance crew, sub-level 2
briefing.report: A maintenance crew sealed the floor after reporting 'cold that moves'. Two of the three came back. Mains have been down six days.

known.text: One surviving crew member is waiting at the stair head.
Plant log reports the chiller ran eleven days against a four-hour duty cycle.

_placementNote:
⚠ THE CONTEXT VERB IS NEAREST-WINS, AND `sourceInReach` RETURNS THE FIRST HIT RATHER THAN THE NEAREST ONE. Its probe radius is `reachMetres + 0.6` = 2.8m, so two sources inside 2.8m of each other means the EARLIER one in this array answers for both — and once that one is logged, `contextAction` offers the later one nothing at all, because the candidate is only pushed when the ledger does not already hold it. Not 'harder to select'. No verb.

So the standard on this floor is a clear margin, not the bare 2m: the tightest pair here is 4.39m (the survivor and the stair-head draught, both authored before this note). Every source is also clear of both door centres, both breakers, the cargo cache and the extraction circle, so nothing on the floor can shadow a pickup and no pickup can shadow the breaker a squad needs.

The five sources added at revision 0.2.0 are SPREAD, deliberately. Evidence that all lives in one room is one pickup wearing five hats: a squad reads the lot in ninety seconds and learns nothing about the floor. The muster board and the charging rack are safe reading in the bay; the chart recorder is in the freight lobby; the crew's imager and the two lamps are up the aisles, where the draught is, and cost the walk.
